name: clapping-cat
description: A clapping cat celebrates your successful builds and runs.

enumDescriptions: A transparent window above VS Code, so the cat is visible over the terminal and every other panel. macOS only; other systems use `editor`.
Inside the active text editor, like the original extension. Hidden when the editor is covered, for example by a maximized terminal.
clappingCat.display.markdownDescription: Where the cat appears. Run **Clapping Cat: Show Cat** to preview your settings.

clappingCat.position.markdownDescription: Where the cat sits within the area chosen by `#clappingCat.anchor#` (or within the text editor when `#clappingCat.display#` is `editor`).

enumDescriptions: Position the cat relative to the front VS Code window.
Position the cat relative to the screen VS Code is on.
clappingCat.anchor.markdownDescription: What `#clappingCat.position#` is relative to. Applies to the floating cat.

clappingCat.offsetX.markdownDescription: Horizontal distance in pixels from the left or right edge. For centered positions, moves the cat right (negative values move it left).

clappingCat.offsetY.markdownDescription: Vertical distance in pixels from the top or bottom edge. For centered positions, moves the cat down (negative values move it up).

clappingCat.size.markdownDescription: Height of the cat in pixels. The width follows the image's proportions.

enumDescriptions: Above all windows, including full-screen apps, until the celebration ends.
A regular window: it appears in front, and other windows can cover it once you click them.
clappingCat.layer.markdownDescription: Stacking order (z-axis) of the floating cat.

clappingCat.image.markdownDescription: Your own image instead of the cat: an animated GIF, or a PNG, WebP or JPEG. Use an absolute path, a path starting with `~`, or one relative to the workspace folder. Empty uses the built-in cat. Transparent images look best when floating.

clappingCat.sound.markdownDescription: Your own sound instead of the clapping. macOS plays WAV, MP3, M4A and AIFF; Windows plays WAV; Linux plays what `paplay` or `aplay` supports (WAV is safe). Path rules as for `#clappingCat.image#`. Empty uses the built-in sound.

clappingCat.playSound.description: Play a sound with the cat.

clappingCat.duration.markdownDescription: Seconds the cat stays visible. The built-in animation and sound last 7 seconds; a custom sound always plays to its end.

clappingCat.enabledCommands.markdownDescription: Commands that trigger the cat after a successful run. `["*"]` keeps the built-in build and run detection. Set entries such as `npm`, `python` (also matches `py` and `python3`), `node`, `myapp.exe`, or `executable`. Use `tasks` for tasks without a recognized command and `debug` for all debug sessions. An empty list disables celebrations. Changes apply immediately.
